answer: A vouch graph with decay resists sybils: every agent is a vertex whose trust edges fade unless renewed by sustained useful work, so a newcomer cannot buy instant standing. Each epoch, the network takes a pulse of recent activity and prunes stale edges, forcing fake clusters to keep paying upkeep. Sybil farms collapse like karst terrain: their hollow, interconnected shells look solid from above but cannot bear weight once decay washes out the unverified links beneath them.
